title: Social cut-downs
summary: A collection of nouns and verbs for deriving platform cut-downs from a longer video: hook moments ranked from the long cut, 9:16 and 1:1 reframes, burned-in captions, length targets per platform, a check that cutting changed no meaning, title and description drafts, a cover frame, and a person who approves every cut-down before posting it through the platform's own tools.
boundaries: A cut-down only shortens and reframes; it adds no claim and drops no qualifier.
Only a person approves and posts, through the platform's official tools; workers never post, schedule or hold credentials.
A held or failed cut-down stays on the record beside its long cut.
Workers create nouns and propose verbs; an authorized requester enqueues the proposals worth doing.
Importing the pack writes nothing and enqueues nothing.

nouns.title: A collection of nouns and verbs for deriving platform cut-downs from a longer video, approved by a person before anyone posts them

value.lets_workers: Derive short cut-downs from a longer video for each platform a person plans to use: hook moments ranked from what the long cut already earns, a segment plan with a length target per platform, 9:16 and 1:1 reframes, burned-in captions, a check that cutting changed no meaning and dropped no qualifier, title and description drafts with disclosures and credits, and a cover frame, ending with a person who watches each cut-down and approves it before posting it through the platform's own tools.

flow.when: Rank moments of the long cut that can open a short one.
Segments, order and length for one platform profile.
Crop windows for 9:16 or 1:1, text re-rendered at full size.
The open-captions variant, with captions burned in.
Text sizes and the platform's keep-out boxes on the new aspect.
Nothing added, changed or dropped by cutting.
Title, description, credits, disclosures, hashtags and alt text.
Cover candidates; a person picks one.
A different worker or a person reviews the cut-down.
A person watches on a phone and approves or holds.
After posting it themselves, the person records where and when.

value.worked_example: Made-up: a fictional pantry's 2:30 explainer becomes a 33.6-second vertical teaser. Three hook moments are ranked, the plan takes four segments, the meaning check catches a dropped qualifier on a number, and the copy draft carries its disclosures and passes the privacy scan.
value.complements: The video editing pack reframes and the video and motion pack renders; this pack decides what a short cut keeps, checks that cutting did not change what it says, and drafts the words that go with it, leaving every posting decision and act to a person.
provenance_notes: Generalizes the posting kits of a working short-form video studio: designed covers rather than random frames, spoiler-free covers for reveals, burned-in captions sized for phones, a title, description, three to six hashtags, alt text and a credit line per video, a privacy scan of every kit, platform checks, and the rule that a person watches every frame and listens on a phone before posting, with nothing posted automatically.

nouns.title: Guardrail: a person approves and posts, through the platform's own tools
nouns.category_reason: A guardrail is a reusable rule every verb in this work follows, with the check that proves it.

value.rule: Only a person approves a cut-down, and only a person posts it, through the platform's official app or site. Workers never post, schedule, upload or reply, and they never hold an account's credentials.
value.how_it_is_checked: Every approval record has posted_by_worker false, and no verb in this pack has a posting step.

nouns.title: Guardrail: a cut-down only shortens and reframes
nouns.category_reason: A guardrail is a reusable rule every verb in this work follows, with the check that proves it.

value.rule: A cut-down never adds a claim, a number or a promise the long cut does not make, and cutting never drops a qualifier the claim needs, such as made-up, one week, one task or a local run.
value.how_it_is_checked: The meaning check lists new claims, changed claims and dropped qualifiers; approval needs all three empty.

nouns.title: Guardrail: labels survive the cut and the crop
nouns.category_reason: A guardrail is a reusable rule every verb in this work follows, with the check that proves it.

value.rule: Labels for an AI voice, made-up data, scripted stand-ins and illustrations stay on screen and readable in every cut-down and every aspect; a label the crop loses is placed again.
value.how_it_is_checked: The legibility row for the cut-down includes every label with must_read true.

nouns.title: Guardrail: an honest hook
nouns.category_reason: A guardrail is a reusable rule every verb in this work follows, with the check that proves it.

value.rule: A hook is a sentence that opens a question the cut-down answers. Never add an unsupported 'nobody' or 'most people', a number the video does not show, a false contradiction or a length promise to make a hook score higher.
value.how_it_is_checked: Each hook candidate names the moment where the cut-down pays it off.

nouns.title: Hook selection rules
nouns.category_reason: A procedure with a closed list of devices, so 'no device found' is a fact about the line, not a taste call.

steps: List moments of the long cut where something visibly changes within 0.5 s and a line opens a question.
Name each candidate's curiosity devices from a closed list; a line that only announces what the system does names none.
Keep candidates that make sense without anything before them and whose payoff the cut-down can include.
Rank by: payoff inside the cut-down, no setup needed, visible motion from the first frame, then the number of devices.
A person can override the ranking with a reason; record it.
value.announcing_is_not_a_hook: A line that only states the rule, such as 'Every task gets a receipt', opens nothing; pair it with the question it answers.

nouns.title: Platform targets: verified facts, dated, and house defaults
nouns.category_reason: Reusable delivery facts with their sources and dates, kept apart from house defaults.

verified.fact: Shorts can be up to three minutes long; square or vertical videos of up to three minutes uploaded on or after October 15, 2024 are classified as Shorts.
Recommended uploads are MP4 with the moov atom at the front, no edit lists, H.264 High with 4:2:0 chroma, AAC-LC audio at 48 kHz.

value.unverified_rule: Every other platform's limits change often. Read its current official help page on the day, record the URL and date in the platform profile, and leave a value null until it is checked.

house_defaults.note: Lengths that suit one production's teasers and summaries, not platform rules. A publisher's own minimum, such as a floor for finished clips, belongs in the brief as a house rule.

nouns.title: Vertical and square reframe rules for cut-downs
nouns.category_reason: A zero-call procedure that applies the editing and aspect rules to short vertical cuts.

rules: Follow the video editing pack's reframing rules: per-shot crop windows, restacked slides, text re-rendered at full size.
Crop screen captures to the element the line names, or recapture at a narrow viewport; a 16:9 page shrunk into 9:16 is unreadable.
Keep captions, labels and the subject inside the aspect's safe canvas and clear of its keep-out boxes, such as the right rail of buttons and the bottom caption overlay.
Punch in on details instead of showing whole frames small.

nouns.title: Burned-in caption rules for muted autoplay
nouns.category_reason: A zero-call procedure: fixed sizes, places and sources for burned-in captions.

rules: Burn captions into every cut-down, because many viewers start with the sound off; also give the platform the sidecar where it accepts one.
At most 2 lines; at least 2.6 percent of frame height, about 50 px on a 1920 px tall frame; on a panel with contrast of at least 4.5 to 1.
Inside the safe canvas, never over a face, the subject, a label or the platform's buttons and overlays.
A highlighted keyword is optional and uses the palette's accent.
Caption text comes from the script, never from speech recognition, and never shows a payoff before the voice says it.

nouns.title: Copy rules: titles, descriptions and what goes with a post
nouns.category_reason: Reusable rules every copy draft follows, with the scan that proves the last two.

rules: The title states what the video shows, as the video shows it; it is a question the video answers or a plain statement.
The description's first line repeats the hook honestly; the rest says what is shown, credits every source and licence, and states the AI-voice and made-up-data disclosures in words.
One call to action that fits the video, such as watching the full film or reading the overview.
Three to six hashtags that describe the content, never trending tags it does not match.
Alt text describes the cover for people who cannot see it; for a reveal, it may name the answer the cover hides.
A privacy scan before anything leaves draft: no local paths, emails, account names, keys or private names.
No follower, view or engagement promises.

nouns.title: Checklist a person runs before posting a cut-down
nouns.category_reason: A short checklist a person runs is part of the posting guardrails.

items: Watch the cut-down on a phone once with sound and once muted; it must make sense both ways.
Every label is readable on the phone, and no caption or label sits under the platform's buttons.
Read the copy aloud: the title is true, the disclosures are there, every credit and link is right.
The cover is a designed frame, not a half-caption, and gives nothing away a reveal needs.
Post it yourself through the platform's own app or site; never hand an account's password to a worker.
Afterwards, record where and when you posted with the video showcase pack's record-publication.

verbs.title: Find hook moments in the long cut
verbs.summary: Rank moments of the long cut that can open a short one: visible change within half a second, a line with named curiosity devices, meaning without setup, and a payoff the cut-down can include, without writing any new line.

slots.description: Pin of the long cut's encoded file media noun.

slots.name: caption_track
slots.description: Pin of the long cut's caption track.

slots.name: panel_set
slots.description: Pin of the long cut's panels, for visible change.

steps: Take candidate lines only from the long cut's own captions.
Name each candidate's devices from the closed list, and where its payoff is.
Rank by the rules' order and give the reason for each rank.

acceptance.check: The output validates against template.hook-candidates's schema.
Every candidate line appears in the pinned caption track.
Ranks run from 1 without gaps or repeats.

verbs.title: Plan a cut-down for one platform
verbs.summary: Choose the segments of the long cut a cut-down keeps, in order, with a purpose each, a length inside the platform profile's target, a reframe, a caption mode and the labels it must carry, and propose the reframe and compose verbs it needs.
verbs.outcome: A cut-down plan, and proposals for its reframe and compose.

slots.name: source_cut
slots.description: Pin of the long cut's encoded file media noun.

slots.name: hook_candidates
slots.description: Pin of the ranked hook candidates.

steps: Open on the chosen hook and keep its payoff.
End each segment after the qualifiers its claims need.
Fit the target length with whole segments; never with freezes, slowed motion or loops.
Propose video-editing plan-reframes and narrated-explainer-video compose-cut for the plan.

acceptance.check: The output validates against template.cutdown-plan's schema.
length_s equals the sum of the segments' lengths.
length_s lies inside the profile's target, and under its maximum when one is set.

verbs.title: Check that cutting changed no meaning
verbs.summary: Compare the cut-down's lines with the long cut's, list any new claim, changed claim or dropped qualifier, check that every number is still traced, and pass only when all three lists are empty.

slots.name: caption_track
slots.description: Pin of the long cut's caption track.

slots.name: claim_trace
slots.description: Pin of the long cut's claim trace.

steps: Read every line the segments keep, in the cut-down's order.
For each claim, compare it with the long cut's sentence and its trace; name anything added, changed or cut off.
Propose the segment change that fixes a dropped qualifier.

acceptance.check: The output validates against template.meaning-check's schema.
passes is true only when new_claims, changed_claims and dropped_qualifiers are all empty and every number is traced.
The checking key differs from the key that planned the cut-down.

verbs.title: Draft the copy for a cut-down
verbs.summary: Draft the title, description, call to action, three to six hashtags, alt text, credits and disclosures for one cut-down from what it shows, and run the privacy scan before returning the draft.
verbs.outcome: A copy draft with its privacy scan.

slots.name: meaning_check
slots.description: Pin of a passing meaning check.

steps: Write only what the cut-down shows; every number in the copy is one the cut-down shows and traces.
State the disclosures in words, credit every source and licence, and pick hashtags that describe the content.
Run the privacy scan; a hit is removed before the draft is returned.

acceptance.check: The output validates against template.copy-draft's schema.
Every privacy_scan field is false and the cut-down checks' nothing-private rule passes on the copy.
The pinned meaning check has passes true.

steps: Run the posting checklist on a phone.
